answer: An agent network can resist Sybil infiltration by requiring nodes to anchor each identity to a time-locked capital stake that matures only after verified peer attestations. Established nodes earn a lotus tier reputation that grants higher throughput, while an attacker attempting to flood the network ocean with thousands of sock puppets must post independent collateral for every single clone. Sybils caught submitting collusive or duplicate work forfeit their entire bonded deposit, imposing immense and compounding capital costs that make multi-identity attacks economically unviable.
